verdict.rationale: Langfuse documents a scheduled Blob Storage Export for large data volumes and API/SDK query access. It is also MIT-licensed and fully self-hostable, so you can own the underlying database, and it ingests via the open OTLP standard, which supports leaving. However, the evidence never states the export file formats or that every data type (prompts, datasets, scores) is exportable. One hands-on user found the bulk retrieval API too slow and queried the database directly instead. Missing for 10: documented open export formats (e.g. JSON/CSV/Parquet), explicit coverage of all data types in export, a migration/offboarding guide, and independent corroboration of a smooth full export.
